sources.title: Effectiveness of job search interventions: A meta-analytic review
sources.authors: Songqi Liu; Jason L. Huang; Mo Wang
sources.setting: 47 experimentally or quasi-experimentally evaluated job-search interventions; country composition unknown from inspected abstract.
sources.finding: The abstract reports improved pooled employment odds and differences associated with intervention components. The index read the bibliographic record and abstract, not the full paper or constituent trials.
sources.use: Pair practical job-search rehearsal with feasible action support; this pairing in Career Junshi is an untested product adaptation.
limits: Component comparisons do not identify an isolated component's causal effect.
The reported pooled odds ratio of 2.67 is neither a probability ratio nor an individual hiring multiplier.
Does not evaluate this Skill or establish current hiring conditions.
sources.jurisdiction: Research, not legal guidance; constituent country distribution not verified.
sources.version: Psychological Bulletin 140(4), 1009–1041; DOI 10.1037/a0035923; online first 2014-03-03. Existing abstract-only audit retained.

sources.title: Job search and employment success: A quantitative review and future research agenda
sources.authors: Edwin A. J. van Hooft; John D. Kammeyer-Mueller; Connie R. Wanberg; Ruth Kanfer; Gokce Basbug
sources.setting: 378 independent samples, 165,933 participants; entrants and unemployed or employed job seekers. Full country composition not checked.
sources.finding: Activity, search quality and employment quality are distinct. Existing audit covered abstract, inclusion/sample description, Table 2 and related results, and discussion of intensity versus quality; not every analysis.
sources.use: Separate applications, interviews, offers and job quality. Inspect targeting and constraints before increasing volume; this review workflow is untested.
limits: Associations do not establish that extra applications cause this user's success.
Does not identify an optimal quota or support diagnosing causes from a short application funnel.
Search-quality findings draw on fewer studies; individual fit and current demand remain unknown.
sources.jurisdiction: Research, not regional hiring guidance; full country composition not verified.
sources.version: Journal of Applied Psychology 106(5), 674–713; DOI 10.1037/apl0000675; online first 2020-07-13, issue 2021. Existing selected-section audit retained.

sources.title: Algorithmic Writing Assistance on Jobseekers' Resumes Increases Hires
sources.authors: Emma van Inwegen; Zanele Munyikwa; John J. Horton
sources.setting: Online labor market field experiment: 480,948 initially allocated entrants; 194,700 approved entrants with nonempty resumes analyzed. About 14% US-based; complete geography unchecked.
sources.finding: Writing assistance increased hiring in this setting. Existing audit covered abstract, intervention/randomization, Section 2.5/Table 1 sample flow and geography, and hiring discussion; no replication.
sources.use: Improve clarity while preserving approved facts. Separating evidence, wording and export is an untested product adaptation.
limits: The roughly 8% reported hiring gain is relative, not eight percentage points or a personal forecast.
Does not evaluate LaTeX, a particular layout, generative embellishment, or Career Junshi.
Transfer to other occupations, countries or hiring systems is unverified.
sources.jurisdiction: Multi-country platform sample; not jurisdiction-specific guidance.
sources.version: arXiv:2301.08083v1, submitted 2023-01-19; PDF title page 2023-01-20. Preprint pinned; existing selected-section audit retained.

sources.title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes
sources.setting: 94 independent tests across goal domains; inspected pages do not establish population or country composition. Not direct job-search evidence.
sources.finding: The inspected abstract and introduction concern cue-linked implementation intentions and goal achievement. Existing audit read the university record and visually inspected scanned pages 69–70, not full methods or trial reports.
sources.use: Offer an optional feasible if–then action. An obstacle fallback and review point are product design choices, not results directly tested here.
limits: Does not establish a guaranteed habit, hiring effect or suitable schedule for this user.
General goal research cannot validate a career-specific intervention.
Do not infer diagnosis, motivation deficits or personal ability from failure to act.
sources.jurisdiction: Research across goal domains; population and country composition unverified.
sources.version: Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 38, 69–119; DOI 10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1. Existing opening-pages audit retained.

sources.title: Toward a Unifying Social Cognitive Theory of Career and Academic Interest, Choice, and Performance
sources.authors: Robert W. Lent; Steven D. Brown; Gail Hackett
sources.setting: Career and academic development framework; participant and country composition of supporting analyses not inspected.
sources.finding: The author-uploaded work's abstract proposes relationships among self-efficacy, outcome expectations, goals, learning experiences and contextual supports or constraints. It also mentions a synthesis; its methods and results were not read.
sources.use: Separate interests, demonstrated capabilities, expected outcomes and actual constraints before proposing one reversible career exploration step. This conversational use is a product adaptation.
limits: A theoretical framework is not a validated job classifier or personal-fit score.
Self-reported confidence does not establish skill, opportunity or hiring probability.
Publisher DOI fetch returned 403; accessible author-upload page abstract was read, not the full paper or its empirical analyses.
sources.jurisdiction: Research framework; applicability to any particular labor market remains unverified.
sources.version: Journal of Vocational Behavior 45(1), 79–122; August 1994; DOI 10.1006/jvbe.1994.1027. Author-uploaded publication page, uploaded by Gail Hackett 2018-05-10; abstract only.

sources.title: Consequences of Individuals' Fit at Work: A Meta-Analysis of Person–Job, Person–Organization, Person–Group, and Person–Supervisor Fit
sources.authors: Amy L. Kristof-Brown; Ryan D. Zimmerman; Erin C. Johnson
sources.setting: 172 studies and 836 effect sizes on preentry and postentry fit-related outcomes; constituent populations and countries not verified.
sources.finding: The publisher abstract synthesizes relationships involving four kinds of fit, employment attitudes and other outcomes, and considers measurement and design differences. Full methods and effect-size tables were not read.
sources.use: Distinguish task demands, organizational expectations, team interaction and supervisor working style; request observable information separately rather than one global fit judgment.
limits: Pooled associations and subjective fit perceptions cannot diagnose an individual's actual fit or hiring probability.
Does not establish causal effects, a personality-based job prescription or validated scoring weights.
The full-text route redirected to the publisher abstract; no full-text review is claimed.
sources.jurisdiction: Research, not regional hiring guidance; sample geography not inspected.
sources.version: Personnel Psychology 58(2), 281–342; version of record online 2005-05-09, issue June 2005; DOI 10.1111/j.1744-6570.2005.00672.x. Publisher abstract only.
